Why calculators can show different results

Same question, different assumptions

  • Your schedule matters: results use the hours and paid weeks you enter — a 2,080-hour year (40 × 52) is only the default, not your schedule.
  • Gross, not net: these tools show pay before income tax, Social Security, Medicare, and benefit deductions.
  • Rules vary: overtime eligibility, the regular rate, and state rules are not decided by the calculator — they come from your pay arrangement.
  • Averages, not checks: monthly and semi-monthly figures are annual averages (annual ÷ 12 or ÷ 24), not four weekly checks added together.

Worked example

$25 an hour, 40 hours a week, biweekly pay, no overtime or bonus.

StepMathResult
1. Annual pay$25 × 40 × 52$52,000
2. Gross per check$52,000 ÷ 26 checks$2,000 a check
3. After entered deductions$2,000 − $100$1,900 a check
4. Federal + FICA estimate$8,038 ÷ 26 checks$309.15 a check

Total: $2,000 gross a check ($1,900 after $100 entered deductions; about $1,590.85 federal-only take-home).

Note: Paychecks are annual averages — actual checks vary with recorded hours and pay dates. The take-home step is a federal-only estimate (2026 single-filer brackets + FICA); state tax is excluded.

What this calculator does not do

  • Take-home is an estimate: federal tax (2026 brackets, your filing status) + FICA + state tax only when you choose a state.
  • Local taxes, benefits, and exact W-4 withholding are excluded.
  • Entered deductions are flat amounts, not a tax calculation.

Biweekly and semi-monthly are different

Biweekly means every two weeks, usually 26 checks in the annual model. Semi-monthly means twice each month, or 24 checks. At a $60,000 salary, those checks are approximately $2,307.69 and $2,500 respectively.

How is a paycheck calculated?

Hourly paycheck

Rate × paid hours, plus overtime and other earnings

$25 × 80 regular hours = $2,000

The calculator models a repeating weekly schedule and averages annual earnings over the selected pay frequency.

Salary paycheck

Annual salary ÷ modeled pay periods

$60,000 ÷ 24 = $2,500

A one-off bonus can be added to the estimated check without changing annual salary.

Gross pay vs. pay after deductions

Gross pay is earnings before deductions. The adjusted figure here is gross pay minus the deduction amounts you enter for one check. The separate take-home line adds a federal + FICA estimate on top of that.

Pay componentIllustrative amount
Gross pay$2,000.00
Entered pre-tax deduction$100.00
Entered post-tax deduction$50.00
After entered deductions$1,850.00

The pre-tax label identifies your input. Pre-tax amounts are treated as reducing both the income-tax and FICA wage bases in the take-home estimate; a 401(k) contribution is an exception — it still owes FICA in real payroll, so the estimate can slightly overstate take-home when pre-tax is mostly 401(k).

Does this paycheck calculator calculate taxes?

Yes — federal only. The take-home line estimates 2026 federal income tax from your filing status and FICA from your wage base, then subtracts that estimate per check. State income tax, local tax, benefits, and exact W-4 withholding are not included, so an actual deposit can still differ.

How does overtime affect a paycheck?

Weekly illustration: 40 hours × $25 = $1,000 regular pay. Five extra hours × $37.50 = $187.50 overtime pay. Total gross pay is $1,187.50.

The tool adds extra weekly earnings at your multiplier, then averages the annual total over the chosen frequency. Use the overtime calculator to examine those hours separately.

Why your paycheck is smaller than rate × hours

Gross pay is only the starting point. A real paycheck passes through federal income tax withholding, Social Security and Medicare (FICA), and often state tax, health insurance premiums, and retirement contributions before it reaches your bank account. That is why a $2,000 gross check can deposit as substantially less — and why two people with the same gross pay can take home different amounts.

The calculator now adds a federal + FICA take-home estimate beside the adjusted figure; state tax and benefits are still excluded. For what each deduction takes out and why, see gross pay vs net pay. For worked after-tax figures, see $50,000 a year after taxes.

Frequently asked questions

How is a paycheck calculated?

Hourly gross pay starts with rate times paid hours, plus overtime and other earnings. Salary gross pay starts with annual salary divided by the modeled pay periods.

How much is a $25 hourly paycheck?

At 40 hours a week for 52 paid weeks, gross weekly pay is $1,000 and gross biweekly pay is $2,000 before overtime, bonuses, or deductions.

How many paychecks are there in a year?

This model uses 52 weekly, 26 biweekly, 24 semi-monthly, 12 monthly, four quarterly, or one annual payment. Actual calendar pay dates can differ.

What is the difference between biweekly and semi-monthly?

Biweekly means every two weeks. Semi-monthly means twice each month. The standard model uses 26 and 24 checks respectively.

Does this calculate taxes?

Yes — a federal + FICA estimate, plus an optional state estimate. The take-home line subtracts estimated 2026 federal income tax (your filing status) and FICA (Social Security + Medicare) from your adjusted pay, and subtracts estimated 2026 state income tax when you choose a state. Local taxes, benefits, and exact W-4 withholding are not included.

Can I choose single or married filing jointly?

Yes. The take-home estimate uses the 2026 standard deduction and brackets for your filing status: $16,100 for single, $32,200 for married filing jointly.

Does overtime affect my paycheck?

Yes. The selected multiplier applies to the extra weekly hours entered. The result averages those earnings over the selected pay frequency.

Is adjusted pay the same as take-home pay?

No. Adjusted pay subtracts only the deductions you entered. The separate take-home line subtracts the federal + FICA estimate as well, plus a state estimate when you choose a state. Local taxes are still excluded.

Can I use an annual salary?

Yes. Select Annual salary, enter the yearly amount, and choose your pay frequency.

Are deduction amounts annual or per paycheck?

Per paycheck. Enter each amount for the check you are estimating. A bonus is also entered for that one check.

Why might an actual paycheck differ?

Actual payroll may use recorded hours, specific pay dates, taxes, benefit deductions, leave adjustments, bonuses, or reimbursements that differ from these inputs.

Why is my paycheck smaller than my hourly rate times my hours?

Because gross pay is reduced by income tax withholding, Social Security and Medicare, and usually benefit premiums and retirement contributions. This calculator subtracts the deduction amounts you enter plus a federal + FICA estimate on the take-home line; state tax and benefits are still excluded. Our guide to gross pay vs net pay explains each deduction.

Paycheck calculator methodology

Visible assumptions. Checkable formulas.

Hourly annual pay is rate × weekly hours × paid weeks. Salary uses the annual amount entered. Overtime is added separately, then the total is divided by pay periods. Bonuses and deductions are per check. The take-home estimate annualizes gross pay plus per-check bonus, subtracts per-check pre-tax deductions × checks for the wage base, applies the 2026 standard deduction and brackets for the chosen filing status, and FICA (6.2% Social Security to $184,500, 1.45% Medicare, plus 0.9% over $200,000), then divides by checks per year. Values retain full precision until display. Read our calculation methodology.

References

The official sources behind the 2026 figures used across this site's calculators:

  • IRS Publication 15-T — federal income tax withholding methods.
  • IRS 401(k) contribution limits — the 2026 elective deferral limit (Notice 2025-67).
  • Social Security Administration — contribution and benefit base ($184,500 for 2026).
  • U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division — FLSA overtime pay requirements.
  • Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employer Costs for Employee Compensation — benefits' share of total compensation.
